Evaluating at x = v_B gives f_A(v_B) = prod_{l in L} (|A ∩ B| - l). The f_A lie in the space of multilinear polynomials of degree at most |L|.

Its Gram matrix G = M M^T has G_ii = |A_i| and G_ij = |A_i ∩ A_j|. Conditions on sizes and intersections become conditions on the entries of G; rank G <= rank M <= n.
- [graph_spectrum] Conflict graph to adjacency spectrum: Make a graph whose vertices are the candidate objects (allowed subsets, group elements, ...) and whose edges join two objects that cannot both be chosen. Valid configurations constrained only by pairwise conditions are exactly the independent sets, so f = alpha(graph). The graph maps to its real symmetric adjacency matrix, with eigenvalues lambda_1 >= ... >= lambda_N. Symmetries of the problem act as automorphisms; a vertex-transitive or regular graph often has computable eigenvalues.
- [fourier_indicator] Subset of an abelian group to indicator and Fourier coefficients: A subset A of a finite abelian group G maps to its indicator 1_A, with Fourier coefficients hat{1_A}(chi) = E_{x in G} 1_A(x) conj(chi(x)) over the characters chi of G; hat{1_A}(trivial) = |A|/|G|. The number T of triples (x, y, z) in A^3 with a x + b y = c z equals |G|^2 sum_chi hat{1_A}(chi^a) hat{1_A}(chi^b) hat{1_A}(conj(chi)^c). "No solutions except trivial ones" bounds T by the trivial count, which forces some large non-trivial Fourier coefficient (a density increment) or bounds |A|.
- [slice_rank] No-solution condition to diagonal tensor (slice rank): If A in F_q^n has no solution to x + y + z = 0 other than x = y = z (for q = 3: A is a cap set), then the function T(x, y, z) = [x + y + z = 0] restricted to A x A x A is a diagonal tensor with non-zero diagonal. Its slice rank is |A|, and slice rank does not increase under restriction, so |A| <= slice rank of [x + y + z = 0] on (F_q^n)^3, which a polynomial expansion of prod_i (1 - (x_i + y_i + z_i)^(q-1)) bounds by counting monomials.
- [probabilistic] Counting to expectation: Choose an object at random (for example each element independently with probability t). A count of good minus bad features becomes an expectation E[X] - E[Y] by linearity; some outcome achieves at least the expectation. - [double_counting] Double counting and Cauchy–Schwarz: Count one set of incidences (pairs, triples, or (element, member) incidences) in two ways: summing over one side and over the other. - [orbit_averaging] Orbit averaging under a group action: If a group Gamma acts transitively on the ground set X and maps valid configurations to valid configurations, then for any fixed window W in X and any valid A, averaging |A ∩ gamma W| over gamma in Gamma gives |A| |W| / |X|. - [gram_rank] Gram / rank inequality. If: M is an m x n matrix over a field K and G = M M^T. Then: rank G <= rank M <= min(m, n). In particular, if G is non-singular then m <= n.
- [triangular_nonsingular] Triangular matrices with non-zero diagonal are non-singular. If: An m x m matrix over a field has non-zero diagonal entries and zeros on one side of the diagonal (after some ordering of rows and columns). Then: It has rank m.

- [diagonal_criterion] Diagonal criterion for independence of functions. Then: f_1, ..., f_m are linearly independent, so m is at most the dimension of any space of functions containing them.
- [self_orthogonal] Self-orthogonal subspaces have at most half the dimension. If: W is a subspace of F_p^n with u . w = 0 for all u, w in W (standard dot product). Then: dim W <= floor(n / 2), so |W| <= p^floor(n/2).
- [cauchy_schwarz] Cauchy–Schwarz. If: Real numbers a_1..a_N and b_1..b_N. Then: (sum a_i b_i)^2 <= (sum a_i^2)(sum b_i^2); in particular sum d_i^2 >= (sum d_i)^2 / N.
- [pigeonhole] Pigeonhole / partition bound. If: The ground set is partitioned into m blocks and a valid set contains at most t elements of each block. Then: Every valid set has at most t m elements. (Equivalently: more than t m objects in m boxes force a box with more than t.)
- [expectation_alteration] Linearity of expectation with alteration. Then: Some outcome gives a valid object of size >= E[X] - E[Y]. This is a LOWER bound on f.
- [hoffman] Hoffman ratio bound. If: G is a d-regular graph on N vertices with smallest adjacency eigenvalue lambda_min (< 0). Then: alpha(G) <= N (-lambda_min) / (d - lambda_min).
- [parseval] Parseval. If: f: G -> C on a finite abelian group G, with hat{f}(chi) = E_x f(x) conj(chi(x)). Then: sum_chi |hat{f}(chi)|^2 = E_x |f(x)|^2; for f = 1_A this is |A| / |G|.
- [slice_rank_diagonal] Slice rank of a diagonal tensor. If: T: A x A x A -> F is diagonal (T(x,y,z) = 0 unless x = y = z) with every diagonal entry non-zero. Then: The slice rank of T equals |A|.
- [slice_rank_capset] Slice rank of x + y + z = 0 over F_q^n (monomial count). If: q is a prime power and T(x, y, z) = [x + y + z = 0] on (F_q^n)^3. Then: slice rank T <= 3 M, where M is the number of monomials x_1^{a_1}...x_n^{a_n} with 0 <= a_i <= q - 1 and a_1 + ... + a_n <= n (q - 1) / 3. For q = 3, M = sum over (i, j) with i + 2j <= 2n/3 of n! / (i! j! (n - i - j)!).
- [slice_rank_general_equation] Slice-rank bound for a x + b y + c z = 0 with a + b + c = 0 (statement unverified). If: p is an odd prime, a, b, c are non-zero in F_p with a + b + c = 0, and A in F_p^n has no solution to a x + b y + c z = 0 other than x = y = z.
